deep.reconstruction:
Folio 137 has no calculations. It continues the philosophical notes 'Fragen zur Metaphysik der Mathematik' from the previous page, which is dated 1825 Dec. 4 at its top. There Gauss defined mathematics as 'the science of relations (Verhältnisse), abstracting from their content'. He also illustrated discrete quantities by the lattice of Gaussian integers used in his biquadratic-residue work. Read in modern terms, the page says the following.

(A) Things in which each element stands in a relation of inequality to only two others have, as their general picture, points on a line. Gauss draws a small line with dots. In modern terms: a discrete chain or linear order in which each element has exactly two neighbours, like Z with its successor and predecessor relation.

(B) If a point can be related to more than two others, the picture is points in a surface (Fläche) joined by lines. In modern terms: a graph embedded in the plane, such as the square lattice Z[i] on the previous page. He corrected 'die durch Linien mit' to 'in einer Fläche die durch Linien verbunden sind'.

(C) A real investigation is possible only for points that stand in a mutual relation by threes (zu dreien in einem Wechselverhältnisse), and where there is a relation between the relations. My interpretation: the relation a->b together with b->c determines a->c. Relations can then be composed and compared, as differences of lattice points (a+bi)-(c+di) are, so that the relations themselves become 'quantities'. Multiplying by i (a 90-degree turn) is a relation between relations. This is the 'transversal' relation idea Gauss made public in his 1831 Anzeige of Theoria residuorum biquadraticorum, Commentatio secunda.

(D) It will be especially important to make the theory of opposition (Gegensatz) clear without magnitude. In modern terms: sign or orientation as a qualitative, order-theoretic notion, logically prior to measurement.

His example is levelling a plane with a spirit level. The position of the bubble in the glass tube, at rest, is fixed by two lines: the geometric axis of the tube, and the line through the plane of the instrument's feet. He struck out 'durch das Verhältniss der'.

The implicit point (my completion) is that the bubble reading is determined by the opposition between these two lines and the horizontal. Reversing the level end-for-end flips the sign of the tilt but not the sign of the instrument error. This is the classical reversal (Umsetzen) principle of geodesy, which Gauss used constantly in his Hanover survey. The page breaks off here.
errors: No mathematical errors are possible here; the page is conceptual and incomplete. It breaks off in the middle of the levelling example.

results.what: Discrete linear order: elements each related to exactly two others are pictured as points on a line.
results.modern_name: Linear order / discrete chain (Z with successor)
results.usually_credited_to: Order theory: Dedekind, Cantor, Peirce, Hausdorff (later 19th to early 20th c.)

results.what: Points related to more than two others are pictured as points in a surface joined by lines; investigation needs triadic relations and relations between relations.
results.modern_name: Planar graphs/lattices; composition of relations (relation algebra); vectors as relations between points (affine structure)
results.usually_credited_to: Relation algebra: De Morgan, Peirce, Schroeder; vectors: Grassmann, Hamilton (1840s)

results.what: Programme of a theory of opposition (Gegensatz) without magnitude, illustrated by the spirit level: bubble position fixed by the tube axis versus the line of the feet.
results.modern_name: Orientation/sign as a qualitative notion; reversal principle for eliminating instrument error
results.usually_credited_to: Reversal method: standard 18th-century practical geodesy and astronomy; philosophical 'Gegensatz': Kant's negative magnitudes (1763)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a known philosophical note. As far as I recall, the 'Zur Metaphysik der Mathematik' fragments are printed in Gauss's Werke, vol. XII, but I have not verified the exact location. They match his 1831 public account of complex numbers as relations between lattice points, and his remarks on 'direct/inverse/lateral' relations. The page offers no new mathematics.

checkable.asserts: Gaussian-lattice 'relation' (difference) between points a+bi and c+di is again a lattice element; illustrates context of the triadic-relation remark.
Multiplication by i is a quarter turn: a 'relation between relations' on the lattice (interpretive).
Reversal principle for the spirit level (my interpretation): readings before and after reversal give tilt t and instrument error e separately.

transcription_corrections: After 'sind Punkte in einer Linie' the manuscript has a small sketch, a horizontal line with dots on it; the transcription omits it.
Line 2 reads 'Verhältniss der Ungleichheit hat'; this is consistent with the image.
The superscript insertion 'einer Ebne' above 'folgende' and 'bei der Ruhe' above 'ist bestimmt' are correctly placed.
There is a faint pencil word at the far right near 'der Füsse', possibly 'Seite' or 'Setz'; the transcription omits it.
The struck line 'durch das Verhältniss der' is correctly marked as deleted.
